approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecular graph by sampling local atom and bond edits, including direct exchanges of aromatic carbon and nitrogen that preserve the molecular formula. It validates each product, rejects previously seen canonical identities, and applies a short memory of signed changes in local molecular motifs. A candidate is excluded only when it matches both inverse signs from the same earlier selected transition. After each accepted batch, the walk moves to its highest-scoring neighbor, even when that move worsens the current score, with canonical spelling breaking exact ties. A separate archive preserves the best observation. Each selected move requests at most four inverse restrictions. They last four completed moves, but a repeated signed motif currently replaces its live entry with the latest transition and restarts its expiry.
approach.novelty: Remove replacement and lifetime refresh when a selected move requests a signed motif that already has a live restriction. Keep that existing entry unchanged until its original expiry or ordinary obstruction release; install a new entry normally once the key is absent. Earlier siblings kept several overlapping origins, extended exercised restrictions, or removed the entire tabu gate. This probe retains one original live entry per signed motif and leaves the gate active. It tests whether repeated reassignment and renewed protection are necessary after neighborhood development. The immediate claim is zero overlap refreshes with preserved original provenance and deadlines; later admission and score effects must be measured. The utility hypothesis is that removing this refresh remains non-inferior.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes its three supplied summary.json and run.log pairs with macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population SD 0.006329100643035156; mean recorded AUC is 0.393353971447165. Its latest-origin overlap rule makes a repeated signed motif replace an existing restriction even when the older transition is still within its nominal four-step lifetime. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen Parent task logs reproduces 435 installations, 1711 selected attributes, all 4545 valid-novel decisions and all 195 actual vetoes. There are 46 live refreshes across 37 installation events: the replaced entries have ages one, two and three in counts 16, 19 and 11. These requests move expiry deadlines forward by 87 restriction-steps in total; that sum is requested extension, not realized useful protection. On the identical recorded accepted history and draw stream, preserving the existing live entry instead suppresses 45 refreshes across 36 events, changes 105 batch-start memory snapshots and 19 matching-provenance results, and changes five admission decisions across four batches: four vetoes disappear and one is added. The added veto concerns an actually accepted nitrogen positional isomer with source gain 0.0002621083644149813, which was neither a winner nor an archive gain. The four relaxed Parent vetoes have no accepted scores. This identifies a real provenance/lifetime interaction without establishing whether refresh helps or harms search. The audit at runs/SPIRAL2/policy/passive_audits/r0013-05-improve-L16/overlap_refresh_audit.json contains source/log hashes and 13081 passing reconstruction checks; it generated no molecules and called no oracle. Sibling n-52759efc37a6 preserved all overlapping origins and changed one evaluated batch with paired mean -0.0007299320044169925; n-d0c3ad3e3823 extended exercised lifetimes and lost 0.007992436088286684. The whole-gate removal n-045725e4628f lost 0.002275 on average despite more local source wins. None isolates replacement of a still-live entry while retaining the gate and one-entry storage.
hypothesis: Remove latest-transition refresh of an already-live signed inverse-motif restriction: preserve its original entry and expiry unchanged, treating repeated selected-transition credit for that signed key as a no-op until ordinary expiry or release makes the key absent.

finding_summary.headline: Keeping old restrictions changed five admissions and failed the non-inferiority test
finding_summary.insights: Latest-origin refresh affects both how long a restriction survives and which signed changes belong to one transition. Preserving an older origin restored one veto against an aromatic nitrogen positional isomer, yet removed four others by splitting newer groups or letting an older entry expire. None of the four newly admitted molecules was selected or improved the best archive, although two beat their current source. Each affected session initially kept the same batch winner; the two endpoint losses emerged only after later trajectories diverged. This rules out treating refresh removal as a harmless storage simplification in this evaluation, without assigning the losses to any single excluded or admitted molecule. The chemistry remains concentrated in the same broad scaffold families, including unusual sulfur bonding, difficult bridges and unresolved stereochemistry, so these admission differences do not demonstrate a chemical-quality benefit. Three passive replacement prefixes stop one molecule short; they support the observed decision differences, not scores for unobserved alternative trajectories.
finding_summary.results: All 48 overlapping requests preserved the original restriction and its deadline, with zero refreshes or backfilled credit slots. On the recorded search history, this changed five candidate decisions across four batches: four vetoes disappeared and one was added. All fifteen task–seed runs completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.521759 to 0.518794, a paired decline of 0.002965 that exceeds the 0.002 non-inferiority margin; population SD rose from 0.006329 to 0.008617. The loss comes from drd2 seed 0 (-0.035615) and deco_hop seed 2 (-0.008861); the other thirteen task–seed scores tie. Mean recorded AUC also fell slightly, from 0.393354 to 0.392994. The mechanism therefore executed, while its utility hypothesis was falsified.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffolds drift into unusual sulfur bonding and dense bridges, with no stereochemical definition
molecular.overall_character: This node produces substituted fused aromatics, aryl amines and nitrogen-carbonyl heterocycles, but much of the late chemistry contains unusual sulfur valences, sulfur-containing cages, reactive heteroatom bonds and complicated closures. All proposal sets have ring-closure-string rate 1.0. Aromatic-string rates are 0.9563 for zaleplon_mpo, 1.0 for deco_hop, drd2_docking and median_2, and 0.7184 for sitagliptin_mpo; these measure presence in a SMILES, not the aromatic fraction of its atoms. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout. Recognizable amine, amide and heteroaromatic motifs coexist with structures that are implausible as routine synthetic targets, particularly the dense sulfur-rich leaders. Diversity is moderate across seeds, while each leading excerpt is concentrated on related frameworks. All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories: each has 900 molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Parent comparison uses n-abcd951ab7cc. Ordered optimizer SMILES and scores coincide in 12 of the 15 matched task/seed streams; differences occur in deco_hop seeds 1 and 2 and drd2_docking seed 0. This is an observation about output overlap, not a mechanism-activation judgment. Heavy-atom counts, molecular weights and ring descriptions below were derived with RDKit from the supplied trajectory SMILES. Potential stereogenic centres are not necessarily configurationally stable, and their identification does not establish accessible geometry. Digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's incumbent.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecule is a 26-heavy-atom benzofuran carboxanilide with methyl groups, an aryl thiol, an aminated benzylic chloride and an N-chloro amide. A more conventional 23-heavy-atom ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide scores almost as highly; another seed favors benzothiophene-linked aryl ketones. Thus the useful chemistry is compact fused aromatic rings joined to a second aryl group through a carbonyl-containing connection. Late molecules also contain partially dearomatized bridged rings and unusual sulfur double bonds. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.2. All three complete molecular streams, including their best structures and scores, coincide with the Parent.
liabilities: The best molecule combines an N-chloro amide, a benzylic carbon bearing both amino and chloro groups, an aryl thiol and unspecified stereochemistry.
Later proposals introduce dense bridges, partially lost aromaticity, N-N bonds or unusual sulfur double bonds. Their graph validity does not establish stability or makeability.
The presence of a relatively conventional indole near the top argues against describing every sulfur-containing molecule as intrinsically implausible; the concern is the local bonding environment.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of compact aromatic carbonyl-linked arrangements is missing from many later proposals, despite the relatively high scores of conventional indole and benzothiophene frameworks.
Stable versions of the leading benzofuran substitution pattern, avoiding N-chloro and aminated benzylic-chloride functionality, are not established among the best examples.
The scores do not identify an absent exact pharmacophore; broader stable arrangements of the observed favorable functions remain unexplored in the leading excerpt.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading benzofuran amide scores 0.41003927643747895, the conventional indole amide 0.39905049777278273, and the benzothiophene ketone 0.393567030299894. The initial trimethoxyindole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. A similarly sized, more open/dearomatized nitrogen-containing ring structure in the worst proposal excerpt scores 0.021532846118034143. This supports compact aromatic organization and carbonyl placement rather than molecular size alone. The final densely bridged sulfur-containing proposal reaches 0.3852230774700024, so unusual closures can still score moderately; neither sulfur insertion nor N-chlorination has a demonstrated universal advantage.

per_task.generated_character: The best excerpt is a large substituted aryl/fused nitrogen-heterocycle family with a carbonyl and thione, imines, N-alkyl groups, a fluoro-substituted amine linkage and a long mixed ether/thioether chain. The best molecule has 51 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 870.8, including bromine, chlorine and sulfur. It has recognizable aromatic rings but a highly unusual substituted carbon-sulfur double-bond environment, and an N-bromo ring nitrogen. The seed-2 final excerpt instead combines a fused dione and aza-aromatic cyclic ether with unsaturated hydrocarbon arms and O-S substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 68.9. The best seed-0 and seed-1 molecules coincide with the Parent. The changed seed-2 leader has 42 heavy atoms and score 0.6003577106518283, versus the Parent's 47-heavy-atom leader at 0.6092182584436399; neither set establishes ordinary synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: The leader combines high molecular weight, a long flexible mixed-heteroatom chain, imines, unusual sulfur bonding and N-Br substitution.
The late seed-2 structures contain O-S linkages and multiply unsaturated hydrocarbon substituents without stereochemical definition.
Repeated similar scores among closely related elaborate structures provide little evidence that their growing chemical complexity is useful.
missing_features: Compact conventional substitutes for the successful heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not demonstrated among the strongest examples; high scores coexist with substantial side-chain and heavy-element burden.
Stable sulfur and nitrogen bonding environments are not consistently preserved when the favorable fused core is elaborated.

The observed gradient does not establish that an unseen decoration or target scaffold would be rewarded; the clear missing capability is chemically controlled elaboration of the structures already favored.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. A rearranged small-ring variant among the worst proposals scores 0.526081691583997, whereas the large substituted leading family reaches 0.6161710037174721. In seed 2, the cited aromatic fused-dione proposal scores 0.5999120578463943, while its more saturated or sulfur-reorganized fused-core variants score 0.541765876888247 and 0.5450350272434115. This indicates sensitivity to retained heteroaromatic/carbonyl organization. Numerous leader variants share 0.6155070237050044 despite changes to alkyl arms or N-bromination, giving no evidence that every additional substituent contributes useful chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules carry aromatic hydrophobic regions and primary/tertiary amine centres, but embed these recognizable functions in unusual sulfur-containing ring systems. The best molecule has 32 heavy atoms, phenol and chlorophenyl groups, an aminomethyl substituent, a tertiary ring nitrogen and a sulfur-sulfur double-bond environment involving explicitly hydrogen-bearing sulfur. Other seeds produce small sulfur/amine rings or densely bridged aryl systems containing cumulene-like nitrogen/carbon/sulfur connectivity. Mean proposal SMILES length is 70.0, halogen-string rate is 0.9966, and cumulated-double-bond-string rate is 0.0598. Parent and Child seed-1 and seed-2 streams coincide. The changed seed-0 best falls from the Parent's 0.8856242185485628 to 0.8500094650652374, with unusual sulfur chemistry and constrained rings present in both.
liabilities: Leading examples contain unusual sulfur-sulfur or carbon-sulfur double bonds and hydrogen-bearing sulfur environments rather than only ordinary sulfides or sulfonamides.
Some successful examples combine small rings, dense bridges, halogen-rich aromatics and unassigned potential stereogenic centres.
The higher score does not establish that the apparent sulfur cage can be made, isolated or adopt a favorable conformation.
missing_features: Stable and geometrically credible versions of the favorable aryl/basic-amine arrangement are not demonstrated among the leaders; basic amine centres themselves are present.
The leading rigid and small-ring structures lack assigned stereochemical configurations, leaving the actual spatial presentation of aromatic and amine functions unresolved.
Neutral SMILES do not establish the relevant protonation state of these amines; the zero charge-string rate should not be interpreted as absence of basic chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl-amine/sulfur-ring structure scores 0.9148143511682032. A low-scoring early acid/amide/N-sulfonyl-amine molecule scores 0.007468397818197266. Later leaders have more exposed aliphatic amine functionality and reorganized aromatic linkages, consistent with a preference for their combined presentation; this comparison does not isolate any single group. A late analogue that replaces the chlorophenyl region with a sulfur-containing nonaromatic ring scores only 0.04252669549740123. Sulfur-rich structures occur at both ends, so sulfur count or unusual valence alone does not explain reward. The benchmark score does not establish measured receptor binding.

per_task.generated_character: The best family is a densely bridged 31-heavy-atom system combining propyl-substituted pyridine, phenyl, an alkene, an N-methyl lactam and an N-O-containing bridge. Perceived cycles include eight- and nine-membered rings; these overlapping cycles do not imply independent simple rings. Other seeds carry larger nitrogen-carbonyl ring systems, thioesters, O-Br groups or unusual sulfur-containing bridges. Mean proposal SMILES length is 61.0. Every proposal contains ring-closure and aromatic text. All three complete molecular streams and their best molecules coincide with the Parent, so the same structural limitations persist.
liabilities: The leading scaffold has multiple overlapping medium-ring bridges and N-O connectivity; synthesis and accessible geometry are unresolved.
Related proposals introduce a peroxide bridge or O-Br substituents, and late molecules retain unusual sulfur valences.
The output lacks stereo markers despite potential stereogenic centres in the leading and late structures.
missing_features: Alternative simpler connectivities preserving the favorable aryl/nitrogen-carbonyl organization are not demonstrated among the best examples.
Stereochemical and conformational definition of the dense bridges is absent.
The leading excerpt remains concentrated on a single bridged family rather than distinct frameworks testing the same functional-group arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. The best bridged aryl/pyridyl lactam scores 0.21196904390980506, while an opened carbonyl/hydrazine-bearing proposal scores 0.12467972074136988. The observed gain accompanies a particular cyclic arrangement of aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl functions, rather than simply more heteroatoms. Closely related N-O-bridged and peroxide-extended variants score 0.20775769309691736 and 0.20647766243219587. A late sulfur-rich cage scores 0.18814867381840605. The score differences do not show a reliable preference for ordinary stable bonding or identify an absent exact pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact in atom count but chemically extreme sulfur-rich cages. The best has 30 heavy atoms, five sulfur atoms and calculated molecular weight 513.64. It combines a nitrogen-heterocyclic dione with carbon-bound fluorines, a hydroxyfluoromethyl thioether substituent, sulfur double bonds, hydrogen-bearing sulfur and dense bridged rings including a three-membered cycle. The best molecule retains only a small aromatic heterocyclic region; other high-scoring seeds have no aromatic atoms under RDKit perception. Thus the overall aromatic-string rate of 0.7184 should not be mistaken for uniformly aromatic leaders. Late seed-2 molecules are nonaromatic sulfur cages with aldehyde and N-fluoro amidine-like functions. Mean proposal SMILES length is 62.8. All complete molecular streams coincide with the Parent.
liabilities: Dense sulfur-rich polycycles contain unconventional sulfur valences, sulfur-sulfur bonds and very small rings. Familiar dione and fluorinated groups do not make the overall cages routine synthetic targets.
Late structures add N-F functionality, aldehydes or a sulfur-chlorine-containing acyl substituent, with no demonstrated stability control.
Atom-count compactness conceals substantial heavy-element burden and complex unresolved stereochemistry.
missing_features: Conventional stable frameworks retaining the favorable compact polar/fluorinated arrangement are not demonstrated among the strongest examples.
The many potential stereogenic centres and constrained closures lack assigned configurations or evidence of accessible geometry.
The observed molecules do not identify a missing exact target motif; chemically independent alternatives to the sulfur-cage family remain absent from the leading excerpt.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best cage scores 0.5903526424693334, while the initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298 and an early expanded dione proposal scores 7.590554525032884e-10. The later high scores accompany changed compact topology, fluorine placement and sulfur-rich composition, but simultaneous changes prevent attribution to a single desired group. Seed-2 final structures range from 0.004199910554494925 to 0.4484554129767839 despite sharing dense sulfur cages; shortening and reconnecting the carbonyl-containing segment in two cited late ring systems accompanies scores of 0.2536619453071564 and 0.4484554129767839. The score therefore distinguishes exact connectivity within these families, without demonstrating synthetic realism or a general preference for greater sulfur content.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading and late molecules include sulfur-sulfur double-bond environments, hydrogen-bearing sulfur in unsaturated cages and heavily substituted sulfur connected through double bonds. Conventional benzothiophene and thiol-containing structures also occur, so sulfur presence alone is not the problem.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not control sulfur bonding environments well enough to keep familiar scaffolds chemically credible.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic generation needs bond-environment awareness that distinguishes ordinary sulfides, thiophenes and other established sulfur groups from unsupported local valence/topology combinations. Stable alternatives should be compared within the same learned structural context rather than banning the element or assuming a score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited molecules contain N-Cl, N-Br, N-F, O-Br, N-O and peroxide connections, together with benzylic amino/chloro substitution. Some remain near the top of their observed score ranges, so reward is not a demonstrated chemical-stability filter.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks control over reactive heteroatom-halogen and heteroatom-heteroatom connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal process would need to preserve useful functional-group placement while providing chemically conventional bond alternatives. Any admissibility or reactivity constraint must distinguish local environments and be evaluated rather than inferred from graph validity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has ring-closure-string rate 1.0 and stereocentre-string rate 0.0. Leaders include dense medium-ring bridges and sulfur cages with small rings and unassigned potential stereogenic centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring closure is not accompanied by demonstrated geometric feasibility or stereochemical definition.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction needs task-agnostic topology and conformational checks, with deliberate handling of stereochemical identity where relevant. Counting rings or accepting a valence-valid graph cannot establish makeability, and not every small ring should be treated as invalid.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One leader has 51 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 870.8 with a long mixed ether/thioether chain; another has only 30 heavy atoms but five sulfurs and calculated molecular weight 513.64. Several elaborate close variants share exactly the same score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently control heavy-element burden and flexible elaboration while preserving favorable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic structural simplification needs to consider elemental composition, side-chain redundancy and flexibility as well as atom count. The data motivate testing compact conventional alternatives, without establishing a universal size cutoff or a benefit from deleting every substituent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The best excerpts recur as fused aromatic carbonyl compounds, elaborated fused diones, sulfur-containing aryl amines, one bridged lactam family and dense sulfur cages. Distinct SMILES often change a side chain or local atom without escaping the same difficult framework.
transferable_gaps.gap: Leading chemistry remains concentrated in related frameworks instead of chemically independent solutions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold-level changes should reorganize learned favorable functional-group relationships into different plausible frameworks. Meaningful diversity needs evidence from the chemistry of scored descendants rather than identity counts alone.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
